newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close lower in modest trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close lower in modest trade.

text.p: *Stocks ended lower as afternoon resource profit-taking accelerated early weakness. Volume 345.96 million shares, value A$558.97 million, 1080 stocks traded, 330 steady, 306 up, 444 down
Australian shares closed lower on Tuesday as early weakness in WMC and CC-Amatil was exacerbated in the afternoon by profit taking in resource leaders.
At 4.20 p.m. (0520 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 17.8 points at 2,366.0. December share price index futures were 19 points lower at 2,379 and at a 13 point premium to the index.

While soft drink maker C-C Amatil continued to suffer after Friday's profit warning and gold/nickel miner WMC felt weaker gold and nickel prices, brokers said afternoon selling in resource leaders BHP and CRA accelerated the day's decline.
"The miners came off in the afternoon with some profit taking in BHP and CRA particularly," said a Sydney broker. But he noted both still held most gains made over the last week.
Market bellwether BHP is still about 6.5 percent higher than this time last week while CRA is about 1.8 percent higher over the same period, despite the day's losses.
Nickel producer QNI Ltd suffered a similar fate to WMC, losing ground after the nickel price tumbled to a two year low in offshore markets and the company issued a profit warning.
QNI shares closed 3.9 percent lower on solid volumes.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about 10 to seven, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trading volumes were moderate while options trade was light after heavy trade Monday with little to attract interest, brokers said.
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 6,408 (5,554)
In other local markets, Australian bonds found a more positive tone on Tuesday on a well received T-bond tender and after merchandise imports for October showed only a modest rise.

By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.11 percent. The Australian dollar's pedestrian rally broke into a jog as offshore demand helped it up 1/4 cent and over an old chart hurdle at US$0.7940.

The initial impetus came from U.S. investment house buying and the recovery gathered pace this afternoon when an injection of Japanese funds overcame a temptation to take profits. It also more than compensated for a mixed set of imports data which, to some, reinforced the case for another rate cut.
By 5.00 p.m (0600 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7941/46.
